title: The Loop and the Brake
endLine: At steady state, the liver remakes only what the gut lets escape.

scenes.tts: A few grams of bile acid help absorb the fat in every meal. How can so little go so far? For water, what left the gut was whatever was not taken back. Bile acids follow the same rule, round a loop.
scenes.narration: A few grams of bile acid help absorb the fat in every meal. How can so little go so far? For water, what left the gut was whatever was not taken back. Bile acids follow the same rule, round a loop.
scenes.caption: A few grams of bile acid help absorb the fat in every meal. How can so little go so far? For water, what left the gut was whatever was not taken back. Bile acids follow the same rule, round a loop.
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's world and colour map without a reset, rearranged (16:9): the same cut-away gut tube with its villi now runs along the LOWER 40% of the LEFT 68% of the frame; faint CYAN water drops still drift through it and sink into the blood band. COLOUR BY CONCEPT, as before: water CYAN; ledger WHITE; gut-lining cells pale grey. New in this film: bile acids ORANGE dots; the liver a large deep RED-BROWN shape; the brake signal FGF19 PURPLE. ABOVE the tube, filling the upper part of the left area: the LIVER at upper left, a small GALLBLADDER sac below it, a bile duct running down into the left (start) end of the tube; the right end of the small intestine marked 'terminal ileum'; a PORTAL VEIN tube rising from the ileum back up to the liver; past the ileum the tube continues as the colon to the 'out' outlet. Whole loop fills about 70% of frame height. RIGHT 32%: the LEDGER from the first film, relabelled: a tall WHITE bar 'delivered a day' on a scale of 0 to 20 grams, a small WHITE bar 'lost a day' on a magnified scale of 0 to 2 grams, and the dial 'captured per cycle'. Tag 'teaching numbers' under it. Hook motion: a small cluster of ORANGE dots leaves the gallbladder, flows down into the tube, travels along it, is drawn up the portal vein at the ileum, re-enters the liver and drops into the gallbladder again, then goes round again, faster each lap; a lap counter ticks. On the question, white text across the top: 'How can so little go so far?' On 'whatever was not taken back', a ghost of the first film's drip at the outlet flashes CYAN; on 'round a loop', the ORANGE loop path glows as a closed circuit.
Title 'The Loop and the Brake' fades in above the liver for 2 s while the question text fades out. ORANGE dots keep circling the loop at a steady pace; faint CYAN drops keep drifting in the tube.

scenes.tts: The liver makes them from cholesterol. Between meals they wait in the gallbladder. After a meal they pour into the gut and form micelles, tiny carriers for fat. From the end of the small intestine, portal blood carries them back to the liver.
scenes.narration: The liver makes them from cholesterol. Between meals they wait in the gallbladder. After a meal they pour into the gut and form micelles, tiny carriers for fat. From the end of the small intestine, portal blood carries them back to the liver.
scenes.caption: The liver makes them from cholesterol. Between meals they wait in the gallbladder. After a meal they pour into the gut and form micelles, tiny carriers for fat. From the end of the small intestine, portal blood carries them back to the liver.
scenes.visual: Follow one ORANGE cluster. On 'from cholesterol', a few new ORANGE dots appear inside the liver. On 'wait in the gallbladder', dots collect in the sac, which swells a little. On 'After a meal', the sac squeezes and dots flow down the bile duct into the upper tube; there they gather into small round clusters labelled 'micelles' that carry pale yellow fat specks toward the villi (simple circles, no molecular structure). On 'portal blood', at the terminal ileum the ORANGE dots pass through the wall into the portal vein and travel up into the liver.

scenes.tts: Four names mark the stations. C Y P seven A one sets the pace of the classic pathway that makes them. A S B T takes them back in the terminal ileum. N T C P carries most uptake into liver cells. B S E P is the main pump back into bile.
scenes.narration: Four names mark the stations. CYP7A1 sets the pace of the classic pathway that makes them. ASBT takes them back in the terminal ileum. NTCP carries most uptake into liver cells. BSEP is the main pump back into bile.
scenes.caption: Four names mark the stations. CYP7A1 sets the pace of the classic pathway that makes them. ASBT takes them back in the terminal ileum. NTCP carries most uptake into liver cells. BSEP is the main pump back into bile.
scenes.visual: Four station tags light up in turn on the loop as each is named, each a plain labelled door or dial cartoon (no molecular structure): 'CYP7A1: make' as a tap inside the liver dripping new ORANGE dots; 'ASBT: take back' as a door in the wall of the terminal ileum pulling ORANGE dots in; 'NTCP: into liver' as a door where the portal vein meets the liver; 'BSEP: into bile' as a pump at the liver's exit into the bile duct. The ORANGE dots keep circulating through ASBT, NTCP and BSEP, while CYP7A1 drips in new ones.

scenes.tts: The pool is about three and a half grams, sent round about five times a day. That delivers about seventeen and a half grams to the gut each day. Only two to four hundred milligrams a day escape in stool.
scenes.narration: The pool is about 3.5 grams, sent round about 5 times a day. That delivers about 17.5 grams to the gut each day. Only 200 to 400 milligrams a day escape in stool.
scenes.caption: The pool is about 3.5 grams, sent round about 5 times a day. That delivers about 17.5 grams to the gut each day. Only 200 to 400 milligrams a day escape in stool.
scenes.visual: A label on the gallbladder and loop: 'pool: about 3.5 g'. The lap counter ticks five laps in quick succession; with each lap a 3.5 g block stacks onto the 'delivered a day' bar, reaching 17.5 g, labelled '17.5 g a day'. On 'escape in stool', a few ORANGE dots slip past the ASBT door, travel along the colon and leave at the outlet; the 'lost a day' bar fills to a shaded band from 0.2 to 0.4 g, labelled '0.2-0.4 g a day'. The dial 'captured per cycle' sits near the top of its scale with no number (schematic).

scenes.tts: At steady state, the liver makes only what escapes, a few hundred milligrams a day. The rest of each day's delivery is recycled, not made.
scenes.narration: At steady state, the liver makes only what escapes, a few hundred milligrams a day. The rest of each day's delivery is recycled, not made.
scenes.caption: At steady state, the liver makes only what escapes, a few hundred milligrams a day. The rest of each day's delivery is recycled, not made.
scenes.visual: A third small WHITE bar appears beside 'lost a day' on the same magnified scale, labelled 'made a day', and fills to the same shaded 0.2 to 0.4 g band. The CYP7A1 tap in the liver drips new ORANGE dots at the same slow rate that dots leave at the outlet. On 'recycled, not made', the big 17.5 g delivered bar glows ORANGE, labelled 'recycled'.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea. A recycling loop needs new supply only for its residue. Capture, mostly in the ileum, sets that residue, and so sets how much the liver must make.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea. A recycling loop needs new supply only for its residue. Capture, mostly in the ileum, sets that residue, and so sets how much the liver must make.
scenes.caption: Here is the one idea. A recycling loop needs new supply only for its residue. Capture, mostly in the ileum, sets that residue, and so sets how much the liver must make.
scenes.visual: On 'new supply only for its residue', the slow drip from the CYP7A1 tap and the slow leak at the outlet pulse together, while the fast ORANGE loop keeps running. On 'Capture, mostly in the ileum', the ASBT door pulses. On 'how much the liver must make', the 'made a day' bar pulses. Label at the top: 'make = escape'.

scenes.tts: Now let capture slip to ninety percent a cycle. Delivery stays seventeen and a half grams a day. How much must the liver now make to keep up?
scenes.narration: Now let capture slip to 90 percent a cycle. Delivery stays 17.5 grams a day. How much must the liver now make to keep up?
scenes.caption: Now let capture slip to 90 percent a cycle. Delivery stays 17.5 grams a day. How much must the liver now make to keep up?
scenes.visual: The dial 'captured per cycle' swings down to '90%'. The ASBT door narrows; more ORANGE dots slip past it into the colon. The 'delivered a day' bar stays at 17.5 g. The 'lost a day' and 'made a day' bars are greyed out with a question mark above them. Question card at the top in white: 'How much must the liver make?'

Predict pause. The question card stays. ORANGE dots keep circling and slipping past the narrowed ASBT door into the colon; the dial holds at 90%; the greyed bars and question mark hold. No other change.

scenes.tts: Ten percent of seventeen and a half grams is one point seven five grams a day. That is about six times a mid-range loss. A modest slip in capture, once again, multiplies the residue.
scenes.narration: Ten percent of 17.5 grams is 1.75 grams a day. That is about six times a mid-range loss. A modest slip in capture, once again, multiplies the residue.
scenes.caption: Ten percent of 17.5 grams is 1.75 grams a day. That is about six times a mid-range loss. A modest slip in capture, once again, multiplies the residue.
scenes.visual: Question card dissolves. The 'lost a day' bar rises from 0.3 to 1.75 g on its magnified scale, labelled '1.75 g a day'; a faint tick stays at 0.3 labelled 'before: 0.3'. A WHITE bracket between them reads 'about x 6'. The outlet leak of ORANGE dots thickens. The 'made a day' bar stays greyed for now.

scenes.tts: How does the liver know? Bile acids taken up in the ileum switch on a nuclear receptor, F X R. It induces a signal, F G F nineteen, which reaches the liver and lowers C Y P seven A one.
scenes.narration: How does the liver know? Bile acids taken up in the ileum switch on a nuclear receptor, FXR. It induces a signal, FGF19, which reaches the liver and lowers CYP7A1.
scenes.caption: How does the liver know? Bile acids taken up in the ileum switch on a nuclear receptor, FXR. It induces a signal, FGF19, which reaches the liver and lowers CYP7A1.
scenes.visual: Reset the dial to near the top and the ASBT door to normal width; the leak returns to a thin drip. Camera pushes in on one ileal cell at the ASBT door, filling about 60% of frame height. On 'switch on', ORANGE dots entering through ASBT light a switch inside the cell labelled 'FXR'. On 'F G F nineteen', PURPLE dots leave the cell into the portal vein, labelled 'FGF19'. Camera pulls back along the portal vein with the PURPLE dots to the liver. On 'lowers C Y P seven A one', the PURPLE dots settle on the CYP7A1 tap and turn it partly closed; its drip of new ORANGE dots slows. Label by the tap: 'brake'.

scenes.tts: So when ileal recovery falls, less F G F nineteen arrives, the brake lifts, and synthesis rises. If it rises enough, the pool holds. If not, the pool settles smaller, where loss equals synthesis.
scenes.narration: So when ileal recovery falls, less FGF19 arrives, the brake lifts, and synthesis rises. If it rises enough, the pool holds. If not, the pool settles smaller, where loss equals synthesis.
scenes.caption: So when ileal recovery falls, less FGF19 arrives, the brake lifts, and synthesis rises. If it rises enough, the pool holds. If not, the pool settles smaller, where loss equals synthesis.
scenes.visual: The ASBT door narrows again and the dial drops; fewer ORANGE dots enter the ileal cell, and the stream of PURPLE dots up the portal vein thins. On 'the brake lifts', the PURPLE dots fall away from the CYP7A1 tap and it opens wider; its ORANGE drip speeds up and the 'made a day' bar rises and un-greys. On 'the pool holds', the gallbladder's ORANGE pool stays the same size (ghost A, labelled 'keeps up'). On 'settles smaller', a second ghost of the gallbladder pool shrinks and then stops at a smaller size, labelled 'cannot keep up'; at that size the leak at the outlet and the drip from the tap match. Schematic, no numbers on the pool.

scenes.tts: So the liver is not the store. It only tops up what slips past the gut. The gut's own uptake sets the brake on that synthesis.
scenes.narration: So the liver is not the store. It only tops up what slips past the gut. The gut's own uptake sets the brake on that synthesis.
scenes.caption: So the liver is not the store. It only tops up what slips past the gut. The gut's own uptake sets the brake on that synthesis.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full loop; dial back near the top, ASBT door normal, ledger back to 17.5 g delivered and 0.2 to 0.4 g lost and made. On 'not the store', the big ORANGE loop of recycled dots glows. On 'tops up what slips past', the slow tap drip and the slow outlet leak pulse together. On 'sets the brake', the PURPLE dots travelling from the ileum to the CYP7A1 tap pulse once.

End card over the dimmed but still moving world (ORANGE dots circling the loop, a thin leak at the outlet, a slow drip from the liver's tap, faint CYAN drops in the tube). Large white text, centred: 'At steady state, the liver remakes only what the gut lets escape.'
